scenario: 设计社交 feed 排序：一个模型要同时预测 P(点击)、P(转发)、P(有意义评论)、P(长停留) 和创作者公平分。
scenario_en: Designing social feed ranking: one model must jointly predict P(click), P(reshare), P(meaningful comment), P(long dwell), and a creator-equity score.
q: feed 排序模型的核心形态和三大支柱是什么？
q_en: What is the core shape and three pillars of the feed-ranking model?
why: 核心是一个模型对每个「观看者-发帖者-内容」三元组联合预测多个目标头（点击/转发/评论/停留/创作者公平）。三大支柱：多任务学习(MTL) 联合优化、专家混合(MoE) 处理内容异质、损失设计对抗指标蚕食。
why_en: The core is one model jointly predicting multiple heads (click/reshare/comment/dwell/creator equity) per viewer-poster-content triple, resting on three pillars: multi-task learning, mixture-of-experts for content heterogeneity, and loss design against cannibalization.
diagram:
flowchart TB
  F["特征: 三元组"] --> S["共享表示"]
  S --> MTL["多任务头"]
  MTL --> C["点击"]
  MTL --> R["转发"]
  MTL --> M["有意义评论"]
  MTL --> D["长停留"]
  MTL --> E["创作者公平"]
options: 每个目标各训一个独立模型，互不共享
一个模型联合预测多目标头(点击/转发/评论/停留/公平)，三支柱=MTL+MoE+抗蚕食损失设计
只预测点击一个目标，其他都不管
用纯规则打分，不用任何模型
options_en: Train a separate model per objective with no sharing.
One model jointly predicts multiple heads (click/reshare/comment/dwell/equity); three pillars = MTL + MoE + anti-cannibalization loss design.
Predict only click and ignore the rest.
Score purely by rules with no model.
optionExplanations: 独立模型浪费算力、丢失共享表示，正是本设计要避免的。
对；联合多头+MTL/MoE/损失设计三支柱，是 feed 排序的主流架构。
只预测点击会诱导 clickbait，忽略转发/评论/停留/公平等多目标。
纯规则无法个性化，也表达不了多目标权衡。
optionExplanations_en: Separate models waste compute and lose shared representation — exactly what this design avoids.
Correct — joint multi-head plus the MTL/MoE/loss-design trio is the mainstream feed-ranking architecture.
Predicting only click invites clickbait and ignores reshare/comment/dwell/equity.
Pure rules can't personalize or express multi-objective tradeoffs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多任务学习：一个模型共享表示同时优化多个目标，比每目标单独训模型更省且能互相受益。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MTL (Multi-Task Learning) trains one model with shared representation to optimize several objectives at once, cheaper than separate models and mutually beneficial.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量分发是否公平覆盖不同创作者的分数，作为防止只追参与的护栏目标之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Creator equity scores whether distribution fairly reaches diverse creators, a guardrail objective against pure engagement-chasing.

scenario: 有人主张给点击、转发、评论各训一个独立模型，分开上线打分。
scenario_en: Someone proposes training separate models for click, reshare, and comment and scoring them independently.
q: 为什么用一个多任务模型联合优化，而不是每任务一个独立模型？
q_en: Why one multi-task model instead of a separate model per task?
why: feed 排序本质多目标。分开训既浪费算力（重复造底座），又丢掉共享表示——会转发的用户通常先点了击，任务间有强相关信号，共享底座能互相受益。MTL 一个模型学共享表示 + 各任务头，更省也更准。
why_en: Feed ranking is inherently multi-objective, and separate models both waste compute and miss shared representation, since users who reshare usually clicked first, so a shared backbone lets tasks benefit each other.
tradeoff: MTL 共享底座（省算力+共享信号） vs 每任务独立模型（零干扰但重复造底座、丢共享）
options: 独立模型互不干扰，任何情况下都更好
feed 本质多目标，独立训浪费算力且丢共享表示（转发者常先点击），MTL 共享底座更省更准
MTL 只是为了省钱，精度一定更差
任务之间毫无关联，共享表示没有意义
options_en: Separate models never interfere and are always better.
Feed is inherently multi-objective; separate training wastes compute and loses shared representation (resharers usually clicked first), so MTL's shared backbone is cheaper and more accurate.
MTL is only about saving money and is always less accurate.
Tasks are unrelated, so shared representation is meaningless.
whenOtherWins: 如果两个任务本质完全无关（用户预测 vs 一个毫不相干的内容审核任务），强行共享底座反而互相污染，这时分开独立模型更合适。
whenOtherWins_en: If two tasks are truly unrelated (user prediction vs a wholly unrelated moderation task), forcing a shared backbone mutually pollutes them, and separate models fit better.
optionExplanations: 独立模型确实零干扰，但重复造底座、丢共享信号，多数相关任务下更差。
对；相关任务共享底座能互相受益，还省算力，是 feed 多目标的标准解。
共享相关信号常常提升而非降低精度，不是纯省钱。
feed 任务高度相关（点击/转发/评论同源），共享很有意义。
optionExplanations_en: Separate models are interference-free but rebuild backbones and lose shared signal, worse for most related tasks.
Correct — related tasks sharing a backbone benefit each other and save compute, the standard feed multi-objective solution.
Sharing related signal often raises accuracy, not lowers it — not just cost.
Feed tasks are highly related (click/reshare/comment same-source), so sharing is meaningful.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多任务共用的底层特征表示，让相关任务的信号互相增强、避免重复学习。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shared representation is the common bottom feature layer across tasks, letting related signals reinforce each other and avoid relearning.

scenario: 多任务底座有两种：所有任务共用一个底座，或每个任务用自己的门控在一组专家上加权。
scenario_en: Two MTL backbones: all tasks share one bottom, or each task uses its own gating over a set of experts.
q: shared-bottom 和 MMoE 的核心区别是什么？
q_en: What's the core difference between shared-bottom and MMoE?
why: shared-bottom：一个共享 embedding+交互层 → 各任务塔，简单便宜，但目标冲突时会互相拖累（clickbait 拉高点击却害了深度评论）。MMoE：一组专家子网络，每个任务有自己的门控网络对专家做 softmax 加权，选择性共享、减少干扰、不用整模型复制。
why_en: Shared-bottom uses one shared bottom into task towers — simple and cheap but breaks on conflict — while MMoE gives each task its own gating network softmax-weighting a set of shared experts for selective sharing with less interference.
tradeoff: shared-bottom（简单便宜但冲突时互拖） vs MMoE（选择性共享、减干扰但参数多、更难调）

rows: 每任务门控加权共享专家

options: shared-bottom 单一共享底座简单但冲突时互拖；MMoE 每任务门控加权共享专家、选择性共享减干扰
两者完全相同，只是叫法不同
shared-bottom 每任务一套专家，MMoE 只有一个底座
MMoE 不共享任何东西，等于独立模型
options_en: Shared-bottom's single bottom is simple but interferes on conflict; MMoE lets each task gate-weight shared experts for selective sharing with less interference.
They're identical, just different names.
Shared-bottom has per-task experts; MMoE has one bottom.
MMoE shares nothing, equivalent to separate models.
optionExplanations: 对；一个是硬共享一个底座、一个是每任务门控软性挑专家，正是二者分野。
两者共享机制不同，不是叫法差异。
说反了：shared-bottom 是单底座，MMoE 才是多专家+每任务门控。
MMoE 共享的是专家池，只是门控各异，不等于独立模型。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — one hard-shares a single bottom, the other lets each task softly gate experts, the dividing line.
Their sharing mechanisms differ; it's not naming.
Backwards: shared-bottom has one bottom, MMoE has multiple experts + per-task gates.
MMoE shares the expert pool with per-task gates — not separate models.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组共享专家子网络，每个任务用独立门控网络对专家做 softmax 加权，实现选择性知识共享。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MMoE (Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts) has shared expert sub-networks, each task using its own gating network to softmax-weight experts for selective sharing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有任务共用一个 embedding+交互层，再接各任务塔，最简单的 MTL 结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Shared-bottom has all tasks share one embedding+interaction layer feeding task-specific towers, the simplest MTL structure.

scenario: 一个 feed 内容类型单一、任务也不多且基本不冲突，团队想要最省算力、最好调的多任务结构。
scenario_en: A feed with homogeneous content, few tasks, and little conflict, wanting the cheapest, easiest-to-tune MTL structure.
q: 这种场景该选哪种多任务结构，为什么？
q_en: Which MTL structure fits this case, and why?
why: 选 shared-bottom：任务少、不冲突、内容同质时，一个共享底座就够，简单、低算力、好调。只有当目标开始互相冲突（clickbait 拉点击伤评论）时，才值得升级到 MMoE 的选择性共享。
why_en: Choose shared-bottom: with few non-conflicting tasks and homogeneous content, one shared bottom suffices — simple, cheap, easy to tune — upgrading to MMoE only when objectives start conflicting.
tradeoff: shared-bottom（任务少不冲突时最省最好调） vs MMoE（目标冲突时才值得的复杂度）
options: 选 MMoE，越复杂越好
选 shared-bottom：任务少、不冲突、内容同质时一个共享底座够用，简单低算力好调
选每任务独立模型，最稳
选稀疏 MoE，专为同质内容而生
options_en: Choose MMoE; more complex is better.
Choose shared-bottom: with few non-conflicting tasks and homogeneous content, one shared bottom suffices — simple, cheap, easy to tune.
Choose separate per-task models; most stable.
Choose sparse MoE, built for homogeneous content.
whenOtherWins: 一旦任务目标明显冲突（点击 vs 有意义评论互相拉扯），shared-bottom 的硬共享会互相污染，这时 MMoE 的每任务门控选择性共享更合适。
whenOtherWins_en: Once objectives clearly conflict (click vs meaningful comment tug against each other), shared-bottom's hard sharing pollutes tasks, and MMoE's per-task gating fits better.
optionExplanations: 任务不冲突时上 MMoE 是过度工程，白增参数和调试成本。
对；同质少冲突场景 shared-bottom 最省最好调，是恰当的简单解。
独立模型丢共享、重复造底座，不是这里的最优。
稀疏 MoE 是为异质内容设计的，同质场景用不上。
optionExplanations_en: Using MMoE with non-conflicting tasks is over-engineering, adding params and tuning cost.
Correct — for homogeneous low-conflict cases shared-bottom is cheapest and easiest, the right simple solution.
Separate models lose sharing and rebuild backbones — not optimal here.
Sparse MoE is built for heterogeneous content, unneeded when homogeneous.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多任务共享参数时，一个任务的更新损害另一个任务表现，尤其在目标冲突时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Task interference is when shared-parameter updates for one task hurt another's performance, especially under conflicting objectives.

scenario: 点击有海量标签、有意义评论的标签却很稀疏，两者共用一个底座训练。
scenario_en: Clicks have abundant labels while meaningful-comment labels are sparse, and both share one backbone.
q: 标签量悬殊的任务共享底座会怎样，怎么缓解？
q_en: What happens when tasks with lopsided label counts share a backbone, and how to mitigate?
why: 标签多的强势任务（点击）会劫持共享层：梯度里它压倒性主导，把共享表示往自己方向拽，稀疏任务（评论）学不好。缓解：用同方差不确定性加权自动校准各任务影响，并给稀疏任务设权重下限，别让点击独吞底座。
why_en: The label-rich dominant task (clicks) hijacks the shared layers, dominating gradients and pulling the representation its way so the sparse task learns poorly — mitigated by uncertainty weighting and lower bounds on sparse tasks.
options: 标签多的点击任务劫持共享层、稀疏评论学不好；用不确定性加权+给稀疏任务设权重下限缓解
毫无影响，两任务自动平衡
稀疏任务会自动主导，压过点击
只影响训练速度，不影响各任务质量
options_en: The label-rich click task hijacks shared layers so sparse comments learn poorly; mitigate with uncertainty weighting + lower bounds on sparse tasks.
No effect; the two auto-balance.
The sparse task auto-dominates and overrides clicks.
It only affects training speed, not per-task quality.
optionExplanations: 对；强势任务主导梯度会拽偏共享表示，需自动加权+下限保护稀疏任务。
标签量悬殊不会自动平衡，点击天然占主导。
稀疏任务信号弱，不可能自动压过标签海量的点击。
这是学到的表示被拽偏的质量问题，不只是速度。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the dominant task's gradients skew the shared representation, needing auto-weighting plus lower bounds to protect the sparse task.
Lopsided labels don't auto-balance; clicks naturally dominate.
The sparse task's weak signal can't override label-rich clicks.
It's a quality issue of a skewed representation, not just speed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标签多或损失大的任务在共享层梯度中压倒其他任务，劫持共享表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Task dominance is when a label-rich or high-loss task overwhelms others in shared-layer gradients, hijacking the shared representation.

scenario: 多任务损失里，点击和评论标签量、噪声都不同，你不想手工反复调各任务的固定权重。
scenario_en: In the multi-task loss, click and comment differ in label count and noise, and you don't want to hand-tune fixed weights.
q: 该用什么方法自动平衡各任务的损失权重？
q_en: Which method auto-balances the per-task loss weights?
why: 用同方差不确定性加权：给每个任务学一个不确定性 σ_k，损失 = Σ (1/2σ_k²)·L_k + log σ_k。σ 小 → 1/2σ² 大 → 放大该任务；log σ 正则项防 σ 无限增长。模型据此自动校准各任务影响，不用手调固定权重。
why_en: Use homoscedastic uncertainty weighting: learn a per-task uncertainty σ_k with loss Σ (1/2σ_k²)·L_k + log σ_k, so a small σ amplifies that task while the log σ term stops unbounded growth, auto-calibrating task influence.
tradeoff: 不确定性加权（自动校准、防噪声任务主导） vs 固定权重（简单但要反复手调、易失衡）
options: 手工给每个任务设固定权重，反复试到平衡
同方差不确定性加权：学每任务 σ_k，L=Σ(1/2σ_k²)L_k+log σ_k，自动放大/压制，log σ 防无限增长
所有任务权重恒等于 1，永不调整
只保留标签最多的任务，其他不训
options_en: Hand-set fixed weights per task and try until balanced.
Homoscedastic uncertainty weighting: learn per-task σ_k with L=Σ(1/2σ_k²)L_k+log σ_k, auto-amplifying/suppressing, and log σ prevents unbounded growth.
Keep all weights at 1 forever.
Keep only the label-richest task and drop the rest.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务数很少、噪声水平相近且你已知合适权重，直接用手调的固定权重更简单，不必引入可学习 σ 的复杂度。
whenOtherWins_en: If tasks are few with similar noise and you already know good weights, hand-tuned fixed weights are simpler than introducing learnable σ.
optionExplanations: 固定权重要反复手调、跟不上任务收敛速度差异，易失衡。
对；可学习 σ 让模型自动按不确定性校准各任务，log σ 防止 σ 一味变大逃避。
恒等权重忽视任务噪声/标签量差异，强势任务照样主导。
只留一个任务就放弃了多目标，违背 feed 排序初衷。
optionExplanations_en: Fixed weights need repeated tuning and can't track differing convergence rates, easily imbalanced.
Correct — learnable σ auto-calibrates tasks by uncertainty, and log σ stops σ from just inflating to dodge loss.
Equal weights ignore noise/label differences, letting the dominant task win.
Keeping one task abandons multi-objective, defeating feed ranking.

termDefinitions.term: homoscedastic uncertainty weighting / 同方差不确定性加权
termDefinitions.meaning: 给每个任务学一个不确定性 σ，用 1/2σ² 自动加权损失，σ 越大权重越小，配 log σ 正则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Homoscedastic uncertainty weighting learns a per-task uncertainty σ, weighting loss by 1/2σ² (larger σ, smaller weight) with a log σ regularizer.

scenario: 监控发现点击任务的 σ_k 被学得非常小（点击标签太多、噪声低）。
scenario_en: Monitoring shows the click task's σ_k learned very small (abundant, low-noise click labels).
q: 点击 σ_k 变得很小意味着什么风险，怎么防？
q_en: What risk does a very small click σ_k signal, and how to guard?
why: σ 小 → 1/2σ² 大 → 点击损失被放得很大 → 点击主导共享表示，正是 uncertainty weighting 本想防的失衡又从另一端冒出来。防法：持续监控各任务 σ_k，对稀疏任务的权重设显式下限，别让点击独吞底座、蚕食其他目标。
why_en: Small σ means 1/2σ² is large, so click loss is up-weighted and dominates the shared representation, reintroducing the imbalance — guarded by monitoring per-task σ_k and setting explicit lower bounds on sparse tasks.
options: σ 小说明点击任务被彻底忽略了，可以放心
σ 小→1/2σ² 大→点击损失被放大主导共享层，可能蚕食其他目标；监控 σ_k+给稀疏任务设权重下限
σ 小只是数值 bug，重启训练即可
σ 大小与任务权重无关，不用管
options_en: Small σ means the click task is fully ignored, so relax.
Small σ makes 1/2σ² large, up-weighting click loss to dominate shared layers and potentially cannibalize others; monitor σ_k + set lower bounds on sparse tasks.
Small σ is just a numeric bug; restart training.
σ size is unrelated to task weight, ignore it.
optionExplanations: σ 小恰恰是权重被放大、点击更主导，不是被忽略。
对；uncertainty weighting 也可能让低噪声任务过度主导，需监控+下限兜底。
这不是 bug，是加权机制的真实副作用，重启不解决。
σ 直接决定 1/2σ² 权重，σ 小则权重大，绝非无关。
optionExplanations_en: Small σ actually up-weights and lets click dominate, not ignores it.
Correct — uncertainty weighting can over-favor low-noise tasks, needing monitoring plus lower bounds.
It's not a bug but a real side effect of the weighting; restarting won't fix it.
σ directly sets the 1/2σ² weight; small σ means large weight — far from unrelated.

termDefinitions.term: task lower bound / 任务权重下限
termDefinitions.meaning: 给稀疏或易被压制任务的损失权重设一个最小值，防止强势任务把它挤没。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A task lower bound sets a minimum loss weight for a sparse or easily-suppressed task, preventing a dominant task from squeezing it out.

scenario: 反向传播时不同任务的梯度方向互相打架，你要在两种梯度冲突处理法之间选。
scenario_en: During backprop, different tasks' gradients oppose each other, and you choose between two conflict-resolution methods.
q: PCGrad 和 GradNorm 分别怎么处理任务梯度冲突？
q_en: How do PCGrad and GradNorm each handle task-gradient conflict?
why: PCGrad（投影冲突梯度）：检测到两个梯度冲突时，把一个梯度投影到另一个的法平面上，去掉破坏性分量。GradNorm：动态重新平衡各任务的梯度幅度，让不同任务以相近速度学习。一个改方向、一个改幅度。
why_en: PCGrad detects conflict and projects one gradient onto the other's normal plane to remove the destructive component, while GradNorm dynamically rebalances gradient magnitudes so tasks learn at similar rates.
tradeoff: PCGrad（去掉冲突方向分量） vs GradNorm（重平衡梯度幅度）

rows: 投影到法平面去破坏分量
动态重平衡各任务幅度

options: 两者做法完全一样，只是名字不同
PCGrad 把冲突梯度投影到法平面去掉破坏分量；GradNorm 动态重平衡梯度幅度让各任务同速学习
PCGrad 改幅度、GradNorm 改方向，正好反过来
两者都只是加大学习率，与冲突无关
options_en: They're identical, just different names.
PCGrad projects conflicting gradients onto the normal plane to drop the destructive part; GradNorm rebalances gradient magnitudes so tasks learn at similar rates.
PCGrad changes magnitude, GradNorm changes direction — reversed.
Both just raise the learning rate, unrelated to conflict.
optionExplanations: 两者一个改方向一个改幅度，机制不同，非叫法差异。
对；PCGrad 处理方向冲突（投影），GradNorm 处理幅度失衡（重平衡），互补。
说反了：PCGrad 改方向，GradNorm 改幅度。
两者都不是简单调学习率，而是专门处理多任务梯度冲突。
optionExplanations_en: One changes direction, the other magnitude — different mechanisms, not naming.
Correct — PCGrad handles directional conflict (projection), GradNorm handles magnitude imbalance (rebalancing), complementary.
Backwards: PCGrad changes direction, GradNorm magnitude.
Neither merely tunes the learning rate; both target multi-task gradient conflict.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检测任务梯度冲突后，把一个梯度投影到另一个的法平面，去掉相互破坏的分量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PCGrad (Projecting Conflicting Gradients) detects conflicting task gradients and projects one onto the other's normal plane, removing the destructive component.

termDefinitions.meaning: 动态重平衡各任务梯度幅度，使不同任务以相近速度收敛。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GradNorm dynamically rebalances per-task gradient magnitudes so tasks converge at similar rates.

scenario: 一个 feed 混杂文本、文章、图片、短视频、直播、链接预览，各类内容的特征分布和参与模式都不同（视频停留是强信号，文本停留可能只是读得慢）。
scenario_en: A feed mixes text, articles, images, short video, live, and link previews, each with different feature distributions and engagement patterns (video dwell is strong signal, text dwell may just mean slow reading).
q: 怎么让一个模型同时处理好这些异质内容？
q_en: How do you let one model handle these heterogeneous content types well?
why: 在共享骨干里插入稀疏激活的 MoE 层：一个学习到的路由器读内容类型 embedding，把每个样本路由到 top-K 个专家（如 8–16 里选 2），不同内容走不同专家、各自专精。只激活 K 个，推理算力恒定，不随专家数增长。
why_en: Insert sparsely-activated MoE layers into the shared backbone: a learned router reads content-type embeddings and sends each example to top-K experts (e.g. 2 of 8-16), so different content types get specialized experts at constant inference cost.
tradeoff: 稀疏 MoE（内容专精、推理算力恒定） vs 单一稠密骨干（异质内容互相拉平、学不专）
options: 给每种内容类型单独训一个完整模型
共享骨干里插稀疏 MoE 层：路由器读内容类型把样本路由到 top-K 专家，各自专精、只激活 K 个算力恒定
把所有内容类型强行当成同一种处理
只保留短视频，其他内容类型全丢掉
options_en: Train a full separate model per content type.
Insert sparse MoE layers in the shared backbone: a router reads content type and routes to top-K experts for specialization, activating only K at constant compute.
Force all content types to be treated identically.
Keep only short video and drop other content types.
whenOtherWins: 如果 feed 内容其实高度同质（如纯文本社区），稀疏 MoE 的专家专精没有用武之地，反而增加路由/负载均衡复杂度，普通稠密骨干更合适。
whenOtherWins_en: If the feed is actually homogeneous (a text-only community), sparse MoE's specialization is wasted and adds routing/load-balancing complexity, so a plain dense backbone fits better.
optionExplanations: 每类一个完整模型服务成本高、丢共享，不如 MoE 在一个模型里专精。
对；稀疏 MoE 让路由器按内容类型挑专家，专精又保持推理算力恒定。
强行同质化会把视频停留和文本停留混为一谈，学不到内容差异。
丢掉其他内容类型直接放弃了 feed 的异质性，答非所问。
optionExplanations_en: A full model per type is costly and loses sharing, worse than MoE specializing within one model.
Correct — sparse MoE routes by content type to experts, specializing while keeping inference cost constant.
Forcing homogeneity conflates video and text dwell, missing content differences.
Dropping content types abandons the feed's heterogeneity, missing the point.

termDefinitions.term: sparse MoE / 稀疏专家混合
termDefinitions.meaning: 在骨干里插入一组专家，路由器每次只激活 top-K 个专家，推理算力与专家总数无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sparse MoE inserts experts into the backbone where a router activates only top-K per example, so inference cost is independent of total expert count.

termDefinitions.meaning: MoE 里根据输入（内容类型/任务）决定把样本送给哪些专家的门控网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The router is the MoE gating network that decides which experts an example goes to, based on input like content type/task.

scenario: 同一个 feed 模型里既有 MMoE（任务级门控）也有稀疏 MoE（骨干内路由），你要说清两者插在哪、按什么路由。
scenario_en: The feed model has both MMoE (task-level gating) and sparse MoE (in-backbone routing); explain where each sits and how it routes.
q: 任务级 MMoE 和骨干内稀疏 MoE 的分工是什么？
q_en: How do task-level MMoE and in-backbone sparse MoE divide labor?
why: MMoE 在任务层：每个任务用自己的门控对共享专家加权，解决「任务间干扰」。稀疏 MoE 在共享骨干内：按内容类型（和任务）路由到 top-K 专家，解决「内容异质」。一个按任务分、一个按内容分，处理两种不同的异质性。
why_en: MMoE sits at the task level, each task gating shared experts to reduce task interference, while sparse MoE sits inside the backbone routing by content type (and task) to top-K experts for content heterogeneity.
tradeoff: MMoE（任务级门控、解任务干扰） vs 稀疏 MoE（骨干内路由、解内容异质）
options: 两者是同一个东西，插在同一层
MMoE 在任务层按任务门控解任务干扰；稀疏 MoE 在骨干内按内容类型路由解内容异质
MMoE 解内容异质、稀疏 MoE 解任务干扰，正好反过来
两者都只在推理时才起作用，训练时无关
options_en: They're the same thing at the same layer.
MMoE at the task level gates by task to reduce task interference; sparse MoE in the backbone routes by content type for content heterogeneity.
MMoE handles content heterogeneity and sparse MoE task interference — reversed.
Both act only at inference, irrelevant at training.
optionExplanations: 两者位置和路由依据都不同，不是同一层的同一东西。
对；一个按任务分门控、一个按内容路由，分别解任务干扰与内容异质。
说反了：MMoE 解任务干扰，稀疏 MoE 解内容异质。
两者在训练时就参与学习门控/路由，不是只在推理。
optionExplanations_en: They differ in position and routing basis — not the same thing at one layer.
Correct — one gates by task, the other routes by content, addressing interference vs heterogeneity.
Backwards: MMoE addresses task interference, sparse MoE content heterogeneity.
Both learn gating/routing during training, not only at inference.

termDefinitions.term: task-aware gating / 任务感知门控
termDefinitions.meaning: 路由不仅看内容类型还看当前任务，防止一个任务的更新污染另一个任务依赖的专家。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Task-aware gating routes on content type and the current task, preventing one task's updates from corrupting experts another relies on.

scenario: 稀疏 MoE 上线后，你发现路由器几乎总是把样本送给固定的那 1–2 个专家，其他专家几乎不激活。
scenario_en: After deploying sparse MoE, the router almost always sends examples to the same 1-2 experts, leaving others idle.
q: 路由器坍缩到固定几个专家是什么问题，怎么修？
q_en: What's the router-collapse-to-few-experts problem, and how to fix it?
why: 没有负载均衡辅助损失，路由器会正反馈地坍缩到总选同 1–2 个专家：被选的专家越练越强、越发被选，其他专家荒废，MoE 退化成小稠密网、白养一堆专家。修法：加一个鼓励每 batch 内专家利用率均匀的惩罚项。
why_en: Without a load-balancing auxiliary loss the router collapses via positive feedback to always picking the same 1-2 experts, wasting the rest, fixed by a penalty encouraging even expert utilization per batch.
options: 毫无问题，路由器就该只用最好的一两个专家
缺负载均衡辅助损失→路由器坍缩到固定专家、其余荒废，MoE 退化；加惩罚项鼓励每 batch 专家利用率均匀
这说明专家太多，删到只剩两个即可
只是显存问题，加显存就好
options_en: No problem; the router should only use the best one or two experts.
Missing a load-balancing aux loss collapses the router to fixed experts, wasting the rest and degrading MoE; add a penalty for even per-batch expert utilization.
It means too many experts; cut to just two.
It's just a memory issue; add RAM.
optionExplanations: 总用同一两个专家等于放弃了 MoE 的专精分工，不是理想状态。
对；负载均衡辅助损失打散路由、让专家都被用上，防止坍缩。
删专家治标不治本，坍缩根因是缺负载均衡而非专家多。
坍缩是路由分布问题，不是显存，加显存无关。
optionExplanations_en: Always using the same one or two experts abandons MoE's specialization — not ideal.
Correct — a load-balancing aux loss spreads routing so all experts are used, preventing collapse.
Cutting experts treats the symptom; the cause is missing load balancing, not too many experts.
Collapse is a routing-distribution issue, not memory; adding RAM is irrelevant.

termDefinitions.term: load-balancing auxiliary loss / 负载均衡辅助损失
termDefinitions.meaning: 鼓励每个 batch 里专家被均匀使用的惩罚项，防止路由器坍缩到少数专家。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load-balancing auxiliary loss penalizes uneven expert use per batch, preventing the router from collapsing onto a few experts.

scenario: 每天数十亿次 feed 请求，要在 50ms p99 预算内做稀疏 MoE 排序。
scenario_en: Billions of daily feed requests, doing sparse MoE ranking within a 50ms p99 budget.
q: 「8 专家 + top-2 路由」这个配置在设计上意味着什么？
q_en: What does the '8 experts + top-2 routing' config imply for design?
why: 这是经验配置不是公式：8 个专家给够专精度，每次只激活 2 个让推理算力恒定、扛得住 50ms p99+数十亿请求。专家超过 16 个对排序收益递减、还更难部署。所以专家数是「专精 vs 部署/延迟」的经验平衡点。
why_en: It's empirical, not a formula: 8 experts give enough specialization and activating only 2 keeps inference cost constant to fit 50ms p99 at billions of requests, while beyond 16 experts gives diminishing returns and harder deployment.
options: 8 和 2 是要死记的硬数字，考点就是背它
经验配置：8 专家够专精、top-2 让推理算力恒定扛住 50ms p99+数十亿请求，超 16 专家收益递减更难部署
说明专家越多越好，应该冲到几百个
配置与延迟预算无关，只影响准确率
options_en: 8 and 2 are hard numbers to memorize.
Empirical: 8 experts give enough specialization, top-2 keeps inference constant to fit 50ms p99 at billions of requests, and beyond 16 gives diminishing returns and harder deployment.
More experts are always better; push to hundreds.
The config is unrelated to the latency budget, affecting only accuracy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个样本只激活得分最高的 K 个专家（如 top-2），使推理算力与专家总数无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Top-K routing activates only the K highest-scoring experts per example (e.g. top-2), making inference cost independent of total experts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99% 请求延迟低于该值，这里 50ms 是给定的服务目标，约束模型算力预算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 latency is the value below which 99% of requests fall; here 50ms is a given target constraining the model's compute budget.

scenario: 面试官让你横向比较 shared-bottom、MMoE、稀疏 MoE、每任务独立四种结构，说清各自最适合什么。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to compare shared-bottom, MMoE, sparse MoE, and separate-per-task, saying what each fits best.
q: 四种多任务/专家结构各自最适合什么场景？
q_en: What does each of the four MTL/expert structures fit best?
why: shared-bottom 适合同质内容、少任务；MMoE 适合多个部分冲突的目标；稀疏 MoE 适合异质 feed（推理算力恒定但需负载均衡）；每任务独立适合完全不相关的任务（零干扰但 N 倍服务成本）。按内容异质性和任务冲突程度选。
why_en: Shared-bottom fits homogeneous content with few tasks, MMoE fits several partially-conflicting objectives, sparse MoE fits heterogeneous feeds (constant inference but needs load balancing), and separate-per-task fits fully unrelated tasks (zero interference at N-times serving cost).

rows: 需负载均衡、有坍缩风险
无共享、N 倍服务成本

options: shared-bottom(同质少任务)/MMoE(部分冲突多目标)/稀疏 MoE(异质 feed)/每任务独立(完全不相关任务)
四种结构适用场景完全一样，随便选
只有每任务独立模型可用，其他三种都是错的
四种都只适合同质内容，异质内容无解
options_en: shared-bottom (homogeneous, few tasks) / MMoE (partially-conflicting objectives) / sparse MoE (heterogeneous feed) / separate (fully unrelated tasks).
All four fit the same scenarios; pick any.
Only separate-per-task works; the other three are wrong.
All four only fit homogeneous content; heterogeneous has no solution.
optionExplanations: 对；四种沿「内容异质×任务冲突」两轴各占一格，正好组成选型矩阵。
四种适用场景差别明显，不能随便选。
四种各有适用场景，独立模型只是其中一格，不是唯一。
稀疏 MoE 恰恰是为异质内容设计的，异质并非无解。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the four span the 'content heterogeneity x task conflict' axes, forming the selection matrix.
Their fits differ clearly; you can't pick blindly.
Each fits a scenario; separate is just one cell, not the only choice.
Sparse MoE is built for heterogeneous content, so it's not unsolvable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组专家子网络加一个路由/门控，按输入选择性激活专家，兼顾容量与算力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MoE (Mixture-of-Experts) combines expert sub-networks with a router/gate that selectively activates experts per input, balancing capacity and compute.

scenario: 团队把排序目标设成最大化 P(点击)，A/B 里点击率短期确实涨了。
scenario_en: The team sets ranking to maximize P(click), and click-through rate does rise short-term in A/B.
q: 只最大化 P(点击) 会引发什么指标蚕食后果？
q_en: What metric-cannibalization consequence follows from maximizing only P(click)?
why: 只最大化点击会把标题党/激怒党排到最前：短期 A/B 点击赢了，但用户取关、28 天留存悄悄侵蚀。这就是指标蚕食——优化一个指标系统性损害另一个。Facebook 的「有意义社交互动」转向正是为纠此，压低被动参与、抬高评论深度。
why_en: Maximizing clicks ranks clickbait/rage-bait first — a short-term A/B click win — while users unfollow and 28-day retention silently erodes, the definition of cannibalization where optimizing one metric systematically harms another.
options: 毫无副作用，点击涨了就是纯赢
标题党/激怒党被排前→短期点击赢但用户取关、28 天留存侵蚀，是指标蚕食；Facebook MSI 转向纠此
会自动提升长期留存，是意外好处
只影响服务器成本，与用户体验无关
options_en: No side effect; rising clicks is a pure win.
Clickbait/rage-bait rank first: a short-term click win but users unfollow and 28-day retention erodes — cannibalization; Facebook's MSI shift fixes this.
It auto-improves long-term retention, an accidental benefit.
It only affects server cost, unrelated to UX.
optionExplanations: 短期点击赢掩盖了取关和留存下滑，不是纯赢。
对；单追点击奖励标题党、蚕食留存，MSI 转向正是压被动参与、抬评论深度来纠偏。
单追点击通常伤而非提升长期留存，不是好处。
这是用户体验/留存问题，不只是服务器成本。
optionExplanations_en: The short-term click win masks unfollows and falling retention — not a pure win.
Correct — chasing clicks rewards clickbait and cannibalizes retention; the MSI shift down-weights passive engagement to fix it.
Chasing clicks usually harms long-term retention, not helps it.
It's a UX/retention issue, not just server cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 优化一个指标（点击）系统性损害另一个（留存/满意度），短期赢长期输。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Metric cannibalization is when optimizing one metric (clicks) systematically degrades another (retention/satisfaction), winning short-term while losing long-term.

termDefinitions.meaning: Facebook 的排序转向，压低被动参与、抬高评论深度和回复链，对抗指标蚕食。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MSI (Meaningful Social Interactions) is Facebook's ranking shift down-weighting passive engagement and up-weighting comment depth and reply chains.

scenario: 你想最大化参与度，但绝不能让创作者公平和有意义互动比例跌破底线。
scenario_en: You want to maximize engagement but must never let creator equity or meaningful-interaction ratio fall below a floor.
q: 该怎么把这个「有硬底线的多目标」落进损失/打分？
q_en: How do you encode this 'multi-objective with hard floors' into loss/scoring?
why: 用带护栏约束的多目标标量化：最大化参与度，同时约束「创作者公平 ≥ 阈值」「有意义互动比例 ≥ 底线」——这是约束优化，不是简单加权和。加权和会让参与度用高权重把护栏项换掉，约束式则强制底线不被牺牲。
why_en: Use multi-objective scalarization with guardrail constraints: maximize engagement subject to creator equity ≥ threshold and meaningful-interaction ratio ≥ floor, which is constrained optimization, not a plain weighted sum that would trade the guardrails away.
tradeoff: 带约束的标量化（护栏强制不被牺牲） vs 简单加权和（参与度可用权重换掉护栏）
options: 直接把所有目标加权求和，一个大权重给参与度
带护栏约束的标量化：最大化参与度，subject to 公平≥阈值、有意义互动≥底线，是约束优化不是加权和
只保留参与度一个目标，删掉护栏
每个目标各排一次序再随机合并
options_en: Just weighted-sum all objectives with a big weight on engagement.
Scalarization with guardrail constraints: maximize engagement subject to equity ≥ threshold and meaningful interaction ≥ floor — constrained optimization, not a weighted sum.
Keep only engagement and drop the guardrails.
Rank by each objective separately and merge randomly.
whenOtherWins: 如果各目标之间不冲突、也没有必须死守的硬底线，简单加权和更省事——约束优化的复杂度只在存在「不可牺牲的护栏」时才值得。
whenOtherWins_en: If objectives don't conflict and there's no hard floor to defend, a plain weighted sum is simpler — constrained optimization's complexity is only worth it when guardrails must not be sacrificed.
optionExplanations: 加权和里参与度用高权重就能把护栏项换掉，守不住硬底线。
对；约束式把护栏设成必须满足的下界，参与度无法用权重牺牲它。
删护栏就回到单追参与度、重新引发蚕食。
随机合并没有明确目标，无法保证护栏底线。
optionExplanations_en: In a weighted sum, a big engagement weight trades the guardrails away, failing the hard floor.
Correct — constraints set guardrails as must-satisfy lower bounds that engagement can't weight away.
Dropping guardrails returns to chasing engagement alone, re-triggering cannibalization.
Random merging has no clear objective and can't guarantee the floors.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在满足护栏约束（如公平≥阈值）的前提下最大化主目标，而非简单加权求和。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Constrained scalarization maximizes the primary objective subject to guardrail constraints (e.g. equity ≥ threshold), rather than a plain weighted sum.

scenario: 你手上有一批「点击率很高、但导致用户取关/静音」的帖子——典型的参与陷阱。
scenario_en: You have posts with high click rate that led to unfollows/mutes — classic engagement traps.
q: 怎么用这些蚕食案例直接改进排序？
q_en: How do you use these cannibalization cases to directly improve ranking?
why: 用对比损失从蚕食案例学：把「高点击但引发取关/静音」的帖子当硬负样本，加一个对比项，惩罚模型把这类「参与陷阱」排高。这样模型学会区分「真好」和「骗互动」，而不是只看点击。
why_en: Add a contrastive loss from cannibalization cases: use high-click-but-unfollow/mute posts as hard negatives with a contrastive term penalizing ranking such engagement traps high, teaching the model to tell genuine value from click-bait.
tradeoff: 对比损失惩罚参与陷阱（学会区分真好 vs 骗互动） vs 只用点击标签（把陷阱当好内容）
options: 把这些高点击帖子当正样本，多推一些
对比损失：把高点击但引发取关/静音的帖子当硬负样本，惩罚模型把这类参与陷阱排高
直接删掉所有高点击帖子
忽略取关信号，只信点击
options_en: Treat these high-click posts as positives and show more.
Contrastive loss: use high-click-but-unfollow/mute posts as hard negatives, penalizing the model for ranking such engagement traps high.
Just delete all high-click posts.
Ignore unfollow signals and trust only clicks.
whenOtherWins: 如果平台几乎没有可靠的取关/静音等负向长期信号，就没有蚕食案例可挖，只能先靠护栏约束或长期价值头兜底，而非对比损失。
whenOtherWins_en: If the platform lacks reliable negative long-term signals like unfollow/mute, there are no cannibalization cases to mine, so lean on guardrail constraints or a long-term-value head instead of contrastive loss.
optionExplanations: 当正样本会强化参与陷阱，恰恰放大蚕食，方向反了。
对；把参与陷阱当硬负样本、对比惩罚，让模型学会不被高点击骗。
一删了之丢掉信息，也无法让模型学到区分能力。
忽略取关就丢掉了纠正蚕食的关键负信号。
optionExplanations_en: Treating them as positives reinforces engagement traps, amplifying cannibalization — backwards.
Correct — engagement traps as hard negatives with contrastive penalty teach the model not to be fooled by high clicks.
Deleting them discards information and teaches the model no discrimination.
Ignoring unfollows drops the key negative signal for correcting cannibalization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击/参与很高但损害长期体验的内容（标题党/激怒党），会引发取关静音。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An engagement trap is content with high clicks/engagement that harms long-term experience (clickbait/rage-bait), triggering unfollows/mutes.

scenario: 你想在最终打分里加入「这条帖子对 28 天留存的影响」，且希望不必每次都全量重训就能调短期 vs 长期的权衡。
scenario_en: You want to fold 'this post's 28-day retention impact' into the final score, tuning short vs long term without a full retrain each time.
q: 该用什么结构来注入长期价值？
q_en: Which structure injects long-term value?
why: 用长期价值头分解：一个独立塔预测每条帖子对 28 天留存的影响，用一个可调权重把它混进最终分。这样短期参与和长期价值解耦，调权重就能拨短期 vs 长期，不必全量重训整个模型。
why_en: Use a long-term value head decomposition: a separate tower predicts each post's 28-day retention impact, blended into the final score with a tunable weight, so you dial short vs long term by the weight without a full retrain.
tradeoff: 独立长期价值头+可调混合权重（解耦、免重训调权衡） vs 把长期目标硬塞主损失（每次调都要重训）
options: 把 28 天留存直接当点击的一个特征塞进输入
长期价值头分解：独立塔预测 28 天留存影响，用可调权重混进最终分，调权重即拨短/长期免重训
只优化短期参与，长期价值不管
每次想调权衡就把整个模型全量重训一遍
options_en: Feed 28-day retention directly as a click feature into the input.
Long-term value head: a separate tower predicts 28-day retention impact, blended by a tunable weight so you dial short/long term without retraining.
Optimize only short-term engagement and ignore long-term value.
Fully retrain the whole model every time you tune the tradeoff.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品阶段明确只关心短期增长、长期留存暂不纳入优化，就可以先不加长期价值头，省掉延迟标签和额外塔的复杂度。
whenOtherWins_en: If the product phase explicitly targets only short-term growth and defers long-term retention, you can skip the long-term value head, avoiding delayed-label and extra-tower complexity.
optionExplanations: 28 天留存是延迟标签、要预测的目标，当输入特征在服务时根本拿不到。
对；独立头预测长期影响、可调权重混合，短长期解耦，调权衡免重训。
不管长期价值就回到单追短期、重新蚕食留存。
每次全量重训成本高、迭代慢，正是解耦要避免的。
optionExplanations_en: 28-day retention is a delayed label to predict, unavailable as an input feature at serving.
Correct — a separate head predicts long-term impact and a tunable weight blends it, decoupling short/long term without retraining.
Ignoring long-term value returns to chasing short-term and re-cannibalizing retention.
Full retrains each time are costly and slow — exactly what decomposition avoids.

termDefinitions.term: long-term value head / 长期价值头
termDefinitions.meaning: 一个独立预测塔，估计每条内容对长期留存（如 28 天）的影响，混进最终打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A long-term value head is a separate prediction tower estimating each item's long-term retention (e.g. 28-day) impact, blended into the final score.

scenario: 长期价值头要预测 28 天留存，但 28 天留存的真标签只有等 28 天后才拿得到。
scenario_en: The long-term value head predicts 28-day retention, but the true label is only known after 28 days.
q: 延迟标签这个问题怎么解决，才能持续训练长期价值头？
q_en: How do you handle delayed labels to keep training the long-term value head?
why: 28 天留存是延迟标签，等满 28 天训练就太慢。用自举代理：先用早期信号（如 7 天回访）当近似标签立刻训起来，再定期用陆续成熟的真标签重训校准。这样既不停摆又能逐步逼近真实长期价值。
why_en: 28-day retention is a delayed label, so waiting 28 days is too slow — use bootstrapped proxies like 7-day return visits as approximate labels now, then periodically retrain on matured true labels to recalibrate.
options: 干等 28 天，标签齐了再训一次
用自举代理：先用 7 天回访等早期信号近似标签立刻训，再定期用成熟的真标签重训校准
把 28 天留存当输入特征直接喂进去
放弃长期价值头，只用点击
options_en: Just wait 28 days, then train once labels are complete.
Bootstrapped proxies: use early signals like 7-day return visits as approximate labels now, then periodically retrain on matured true labels.
Feed 28-day retention as an input feature directly.
Abandon the long-term value head and use only clicks.
optionExplanations: 干等 28 天让模型迭代慢一个月，跟不上产品节奏。
对；7 天回访等代理先撑起训练，成熟真标签再定期校准，既快又逐步准。
延迟标签是要预测的目标，不能当输入特征（服务时拿不到）。
放弃长期价值头就回到单追短期、重新蚕食留存。
optionExplanations_en: Waiting 28 days slows iteration by a month, out of step with product pace.
Correct — proxies like 7-day return visits carry training now, and matured labels periodically recalibrate — fast and increasingly accurate.
The delayed label is the prediction target, not an input feature (unavailable at serving).
Abandoning the head returns to chasing short-term and re-cannibalizing retention.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要等一段时间才知道真值的标签（如 28 天留存），无法立即用于训练。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delayed label is one whose true value is known only after a delay (e.g. 28-day retention), unusable for immediate training.

termDefinitions.term: bootstrapped proxy / 自举代理标签
termDefinitions.meaning: 用早期可得信号（7 天回访）近似延迟标签先训练，待真标签成熟再校准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bootstrapped proxy uses an early available signal (7-day return) to approximate a delayed label for training now, recalibrated when the true label matures.

scenario: 多任务训练里，点击任务的 σ_k 相对其他任务变得非常小。
scenario_en: In multi-task training, the click task's σ_k becomes very small relative to other tasks.
q: 点击 σ_k 相对变小，会对指标蚕食产生什么直接影响？
q_en: What's the direct cannibalization effect of a relatively small click σ_k?
why: σ 小 → 1/2σ² 大 → 点击损失被上调 → 点击主导共享表示 → 可能造成指标蚕食（把标题党排前，伤评论/留存）。所以监控 σ_k 不只是数值卫生，它直接关系到会不会重新滑向单追点击。
why_en: Small σ means the click loss is up-weighted, so click dominates the shared representation and can cause cannibalization, which is why monitoring σ_k directly bears on whether you slide back into chasing clicks.
tradeoff: 监控并约束点击 σ（防主导蚕食） vs 放任 σ 自由变小（点击独吞底座、蚕食其他目标）
options: 点击损失被上调、点击主导共享表示，可能造成指标蚕食（标题党排前伤评论/留存）
点击任务被彻底关掉，其他目标独占
对指标蚕食毫无影响，σ 只是内部数值
会让所有任务权重同时变大，整体更强
options_en: Click loss is up-weighted and click dominates the shared representation, potentially cannibalizing (clickbait ranked first, harming comments/retention).
The click task is fully switched off, letting others dominate.
No effect on cannibalization; σ is just an internal number.
It raises all task weights together, strengthening everything.
whenOtherWins: 如果点击本就是当前阶段有意为之的主目标、且已有护栏约束顶住留存底线，那点击 σ 小可以接受——护栏在，就不会真的蚕食失控。
whenOtherWins_en: If click is deliberately the phase's primary objective and guardrail constraints already hold the retention floor, a small click σ is acceptable — the guardrails keep cannibalization in check.
optionExplanations: 对；σ 小放大点击、主导底座，正是蚕食的机制入口，需监控约束。
σ 小是放大点击不是关掉它，方向理解错了。
σ 直接决定权重、影响谁主导，与蚕食强相关，不是无关数值。
σ 小只放大点击这一个任务，不是所有任务一起变大。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — small σ amplifies click and dominates the bottom, the entry point to cannibalization, needing monitoring.
Small σ amplifies click, not switches it off — misread direction.
σ sets the weight and who dominates, strongly tied to cannibalization, not an inert number.
Small σ amplifies only the click task, not all tasks together.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同方差加权里每个任务的可学习不确定性，σ 越小该任务损失权重 1/2σ² 越大、越主导。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sigma (σ_k) is each task's learnable uncertainty in homoscedastic weighting; a smaller σ means a larger 1/2σ² weight and more dominance.

q: 把 feed 排序模型「从特征到最终分」的层次按正确顺序排列：
q_en: Order the feed-ranking model from features to final score:
steps: 共享 embedding：把三元组特征压成共享表示
特征向量：批特征+流式特征拼成输入
最终分：约束标量化（参与 subject to 公平/有意义互动护栏）+ 长期价值头混合
稀疏 MoE 层：按内容类型+任务路由到专家
每任务门控+塔：点击/转发/评论/停留/公平/长期价值各出一头
why: 顺序：特征向量 → 共享 embedding → 稀疏 MoE（内容+任务路由）→ 每任务门控+塔出多头 → 最终分（约束标量化+长期价值头混合）。损失用不确定性加权+PCGrad。这是「特征→专家→任务→打分」的分层结构。
why_en: Order: feature vector, shared embedding, sparse MoE (content+task routing), per-task gating+towers for the heads, then final score by constrained scalarization plus the long-term value head.
diagram:
flowchart TB F["特征向量"] --> E["共享 embedding"] E --> M["稀疏 MoE
内容+任务路由"] M --> T["每任务门控+塔"] T --> S["最终分
约束标量化+长期价值头"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 实时更新的特征（如刚刚的互动），与离线批特征拼成模型输入向量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A streaming feature updates in real time (e.g. a just-now interaction), joined with offline batch features into the input vector.

The final score uses guardrail {{constrained scalarization}} (engagement subject to equity/meaningful interaction), blending in the {{long-term value}} head.

why_en: The recipe: uncertainty weighting to balance tasks, PCGrad to resolve conflict, constrained scalarization for guardrails, and a long-term value head to decouple horizons.

scenario: 设计 MMoE 时要定专家子网络的数量，团队问「几个专家合适」。
scenario_en: Designing MMoE, the team asks how many expert sub-networks are appropriate.
q: MMoE 用「4–8 个小 MLP 专家」这个量级意味着什么？
q_en: What does MMoE's '4-8 small MLP experts' magnitude imply?
why: 4–8 是经验量级不是公式：专家太少不足以覆盖不同任务偏好的子空间，太多则参数膨胀、门控更难学、收益递减。每个专家是个小 MLP，让不同任务的门控能挑不同专家组合（点击靠 1&3、评论靠 2&4），实现选择性共享。
why_en: 4-8 is an empirical count, not a formula: too few can't cover different tasks' preferred subspaces while too many inflate params and make gating harder with diminishing returns, and each small MLP expert lets task gates pick different combinations.
options: 4–8 是要死记的硬数字，考点就是背它
经验量级：太少覆盖不了不同任务子空间、太多参数膨胀门控难学收益递减，小 MLP 专家供各任务门控选择性组合
说明专家越多越好，冲到几百个最佳
专家数与门控学习难度无关，随便设
options_en: 4-8 is a hard number to memorize.
Empirical: too few can't cover task subspaces, too many inflate params and make gating hard with diminishing returns; small MLP experts let task gates combine selectively.
More experts are always best; push to hundreds.
Expert count is unrelated to gating difficulty; set anything.

scenario: 稀疏 MoE 的路由器只看内容类型、不看当前是哪个任务，多个任务共用同一批专家。
scenario_en: The sparse MoE router reads only content type, not which task, and multiple tasks share the same experts.
q: 路由只按内容、不感知任务会出什么问题？
q_en: What goes wrong if routing reads only content, not task?
why: 只按内容路由，多个任务会更新同一批专家，一个任务的更新可能污染另一个任务依赖的专家（点击的更新拽坏了评论所倚重的专家）。所以路由要同时条件于内容类型和任务（任务感知门控），把不同任务对专家的诉求隔开。
why_en: Content-only routing has multiple tasks updating the same experts, so one task's updates can corrupt experts another relies on, which is why routing must condition on both content type and task (task-aware gating).
options: 毫无影响，任务信息对路由没用
多任务更新同批专家、一个任务的更新污染另一个任务依赖的专家；应让路由同时条件于内容类型和任务
会让路由更快，是纯优化
只影响显存，不影响任务质量
options_en: No effect; task info is useless for routing.
Multiple tasks update the same experts so one task's updates corrupt experts another relies on; routing should condition on content type AND task.
It makes routing faster, a pure optimization.
It only affects memory, not task quality.
optionExplanations: 任务信息对隔离专家很关键，忽略它会让任务互相污染。
对；任务感知门控让不同任务的诉求走不同专家，避免更新互相破坏。
这不是速度问题，是任务间污染的质量问题。
污染直接伤各任务预测质量，不只是显存。
optionExplanations_en: Task info is key to isolating experts; ignoring it lets tasks pollute each other.
Correct — task-aware gating routes different tasks' needs to different experts, avoiding destructive cross-updates.
It's not a speed issue but a cross-task pollution quality issue.
Pollution directly harms per-task prediction quality, not just memory.

termDefinitions.term: task-aware routing / 任务感知路由
termDefinitions.meaning: 路由器同时依据内容类型和当前任务选专家，防止任务间通过共享专家互相污染。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Task-aware routing picks experts by both content type and current task, preventing cross-task pollution through shared experts.

scenario: 你担心加更多专家会让每次推理都变慢，撑不住 50ms p99。
scenario_en: You worry more experts slow every inference and blow the 50ms p99.
q: 为什么稀疏 top-K MoE 能在增加专家的同时保持推理算力恒定？
q_en: Why does sparse top-K MoE keep inference cost constant as experts grow?
why: 因为每个样本只激活 top-K 个专家（如 8–16 里选 2），不管总共有多少专家，每次前向都只跑 K 个。总容量随专家数增长，但推理算力只跟 K 走——这就是稀疏激活「涨容量不涨算力」的关键，像分诊：每个病人只见 16 位专科里的 2 位。
why_en: Because each example activates only top-K experts (e.g. 2 of 8-16), so no matter the total, each forward runs just K, letting capacity grow with expert count while inference cost tracks only K.
tradeoff: 稀疏 top-K（涨容量不涨算力但需负载均衡） vs 稠密全激活（算力随宽度线性涨）
options: 因为专家越多模型自动变快
每样本只激活 top-K 个专家，前向只跑 K 个，总容量涨但推理算力只跟 K 走
因为稀疏 MoE 不做任何前向计算
因为专家共享全部权重，等于只有一个专家
options_en: Because more experts auto-speed the model.
Each example activates only top-K experts, so the forward runs just K — capacity grows with expert count while inference cost tracks only K.
Because sparse MoE does no forward compute.
Because experts share all weights, equal to one expert.
whenOtherWins: 如果专家数很少、且每个都很小，稠密全激活（每次跑全部专家）的算力也不高，这时不必上稀疏路由的负载均衡复杂度。
whenOtherWins_en: If experts are few and tiny, dense full activation is cheap enough, so you needn't take on sparse routing's load-balancing complexity.
optionExplanations: 专家多不会自动变快，是靠只激活 K 个才保持算力恒定。
对；top-K 只跑 K 个专家，容量与算力解耦，正是稀疏激活的核心。
稀疏 MoE 照样做前向，只是只算被选中的 K 个专家。
专家各有独立权重专精不同信号，不等于一个专家。
optionExplanations_en: More experts don't auto-speed; constant cost comes from activating only K.
Correct — top-K runs only K experts, decoupling capacity from compute, the essence of sparse activation.
Sparse MoE still forwards, just over the selected K experts.
Experts have distinct weights specializing in different signals, not one expert.

termDefinitions.term: constant inference cost / 恒定推理算力
termDefinitions.meaning: 稀疏 MoE 每次只算 top-K 个专家，推理算力与专家总数无关，只随 K 变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Constant inference cost means sparse MoE computes only top-K experts per example, so inference is independent of total experts and scales with K.
